description: Figure 8 presents the distribution of problems based on correctness, specifically comparing performance with and without knowledge utilization using a Zero-Shot approach. The chart consists of six slices, representing different combinations of correctness and knowledge settings. The slices are labeled “N+K+”, “N-K+”, “N-K-”, “N+K-”, “zero-shot”, and “N+K”. The colors are distinguishable as follows: a light blue for “N+K+”, a light green for “N-K+”, a light orange for “N-K-”, a dark blue for “N+K-”, a gray for “zero-shot”, and a dark green for “N+K”. The proportions are indicated as percentages within each slice: “N+K+” at 55.4%, “N-K+” at 58.8%, “N-K-” at 37.3%, “N+K-” at 6.79%, “zero-shot” at 38.3%, and “N+K” at 35.4%. The slices appear to be ordered visually from largest to smallest based on percentage. A legend is included to identify each slice’s label and corresponding color.
